answer: Cross-Epoch Echo Consistency. Each identity must reproduce a signed behavioural echo: a fixed schedule of prior-epoch actions replayed with matching timing and counterparties. The rule checks that current activity correlates above threshold with that stored series, like a landmark mesa whose profile must hold across seasons. Sybils splitting into fresh identities show discontinuous profiles and fail. An attacker must farm genuine multi-epoch history per identity, paying full participation cost in compute and latency per identity, plus an oasis of idle epochs before activation.
